judgment_calls.text: AC-MIG-2's diff check (git diff da36c2b..HEAD -- src/marmot/device-sync.ts src/store/task-store.tsx) shows exactly ONE added control-flow-branch (a single ConditionalExpression: `isEngineReadPathEnabled() ? {projection: engineHookState.projection, loading: ...} : {projection: state, loading}`), zero removed, net +1 -- NOT <= 0. This is deliberate and, per this story's brief, the surfaced design tension: a genuine runtime toggle (VQ-S9-001/006 require BOTH branches functionally reachable, not a dead-code-eliminated constant) requires SOME conditional construct to select between two data sources; there is no removable/relocatable branch available inside task-store.tsx to offset it (the file was diff-identical to the da36c2b baseline before this story -- confirmed via `git diff da36c2b -- src/store/task-store.tsx` returning empty prior to this story's edits). The design satisfies the brief's second escape valve instead ('structured so it is not net-new branching... the flag selects a data source that is then consumed by the SAME downstream code, not a duplicated branch tree'): exactly one ConditionalExpression in the whole file, selecting a {projection, loading} pair that flows into the SAME single Array.from(...values()) call and the SAME single <TaskStoreContext.Provider> JSX -- never two parallel render/branch trees. Everything else that could look like a second branch (readyForEngine's `Boolean(x) || Boolean(y && z)`, the JSX `{readyForEngine && <EngineTaskBridge/>}` conditional-render, six `??` nullish-coalescing uses in the interim persistence adapter, and one TS optional-property `?:` marker on engineIngestSourceOverride) is NOT an if/switch/ternary token and was verified NOT to match the AC's own literal vocabulary via `grep -E '\bif\s*\(|\bswitch\s*\(' ` (zero hits, added or removed) -- only genuinely counting `?`/`:` ternary tokens catches the one real conditional. Flagged to the lead in this story's return rather than silently building around it.

receive-engine.ts's PersistenceAdapter has 10 methods; S4's raw-event-log-store.ts implements exactly 4 (appendFact/loadFacts/appendAcceptedEvent/loadAcceptedEvents). The remaining 6 (saveCheckpoint/loadCheckpoint/saveDeferredIds/loadDeferredIds/acceptDeferredFact/clearGroupState) are explicitly S11's deliverable (checkpoint-store.ts/deferred-store.ts do not exist in this repo as of S9), and S11 is sequenced AFTER S9 in both stories.json's dependency_notes and spec.md's own Phase-4-before-Phase-7 migration order. Wiring a genuinely-functioning engine into task-store.tsx (per this story's explicit brief) therefore required a decision the docs do not settle. Resolved as an implementation-detail default (not escalated -- no product-behavior change: the flag defaults OFF, and this only affects behavior when a developer/test opts the flag ON before S11 lands) rather than an AWAITING_SPECIFICATION halt: createInterimEnginePersistenceAdapter() delegates the 4 real methods to the real S4 store and supplies session-scoped, non-durable in-memory Maps for the other 6, mirroring the exact shape already reviewed and landed in react-engine-hooks.test.tsx's createInMemoryPersistenceAdapter. Safety argument: ENGINE_START_OPTIONS is hardcoded to {origin:'welcome'} (see next judgment call), and receive-engine.ts's start() only calls persistence.loadCheckpoint for origin:'restored' -- so this interim adapter's non-durability never gates S9's read-path-equivalence claim (VQ-S9-004, same-session, no-crash-recovery scope). Zero if/switch/ternary in the adapter itself (verified in the AC-MIG-2 diff).

EngineTaskBridge always calls engine.start({origin:'welcome'}), never 'restored'. Rationale: 'restored' origin's checkpoint-driven recovering path (receive-engine.ts's loadCheckpoint + isValidCheckpoint gate) is explicitly S11 territory per stories.json ('handles the malformed/unreadable-checkpoint-at-restart failure mode... never escalate to reset()') -- meaning its absent/malformed-checkpoint handling is not yet a hardened, tested contract. 'welcome' origin's FSM path (L2 -> joining -> catching_up -> live) is already fully covered by S5/S6/S8's test suites and never touches loadCheckpoint at all. Using 'welcome' universally is a documented interim simplification for S9's read-path wiring; correct origin detection (mirroring task-store.tsx's own isGroupJoinedFromWelcome() check, already used for the legacy bootstrap gate) is left for a future story once S11's recovering path is hardened. Does not affect AC-MIG-2 branch count (module-level constant, not a conditional).

TaskStoreProviderProps gains an optional engineIngestSourceOverride?: IngestSource, documented production-callers-must-leave-undefined. Chosen over a window.__notestrTest*-style global hook (this file's established e2e-test-hook idiom) because that idiom's hooks are registered inside a useEffect that only runs AFTER mount -- too late for a unit test that needs to inject a fixture IngestSource BEFORE TaskStoreProvider's own effect calls createEngine(). A component prop is the correct DI seam for mount-time substitution; a window hook is correct for post-mount e2e interaction (different problem). readyForEngine (`Boolean(engineIngestSourceOverride) || Boolean(group && client && signer && pubkey)`) lets the test mount EngineTaskBridge without waiting for real marmot deps, matching the exact 'mock IngestSource + origin:welcome' recipe already proven in react-engine-hooks.test.tsx's AC-INV-4 suite.
